title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Houston, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Montgomery Processing Center (MPC)

IHSC evaluated the detainee and cleared him of any visible injuries. IHSC ordered the detainee to be transported to a local hospital in Conroe, Texas, for further assessment.

On April 19, 2024, the detainee became disruptive, began to throw chairs, and started to destroy a unit cell. NWIPC staff directed the detainee to submit to restraints and the detainee failed to comply. NWIPC staff assisted the detainee to the ground and applied the restraints to gain compliance. NWIPC staff reported a small laceration to the detainee's finger from his attempt to break a window, NWIPC staff did not report any injuries. ERO Leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Houston, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), IAH Secure Adult Detention Center (IAH)
narrative: On April 24, 2024, ERO Houston reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) on a Nicaraguan national detainee while housed at the LAH in Livingston, Texas. On April 23, 2024, LAH staff encountered the detainee after he destroyed a wall mounted phone located in his holding cell and observed him place broken pieces of the phone in his mouth and ingest them. LAH staff gave the detainee multiple commands to stop swallowing the broken phone pieces, but the detainee refused to comply with LAH staff commands. LAH staff deployed OC spray into the detainees holding cell. After the exposure to OC, the detainee continued to refuse LAH staff commands. LAH staff entered the holding cell, placed the detainee in hand restraints, and removed him from the cell. LAH staff escorted the detainee to the medical department for decontamination protocols and medical assessment. IHSC ordered the detainee to be transported to a local hospital for further assessment.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Houston, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Montgomery Processing Center (MPC)
narrative: On April 24, 2024, ERO Houston reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray, on multiple detainees housed at the MPC in Conroe, Texas. On April 23, 2024, multiple detainees were engaged in a fight during afternoon meal service. MPC staff gave the detainees multiple commands to stop but they refused. MPC staff deployed OC spray after multiple attempts to gain compliance were unsuccessful. Of the detainees engaged in the fight, two received direct exposure to OC and required assistance to initiate decontamination protocols by utilizing the shower and fresh air. A third detainee, who attempted to stop the fight, experienced a mild exposure to OC. The detainee decontaminated on his own after receiving a change of clothing and instructions on how to decontaminate from MPC staff. All detainees involved in the fighting stopped and submitted to hand restraints after the exposure of OC. IHSC evaluated the detainees exposed to the OC and medically cleared them. MPC staff placed the detainees involved in the fighting in the MPC Restricted Housing Unit pending disciplinary hearings. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Atlanta, Stewart Detention Center (SDC)
narrative: On April 25, 2024, ERO Atlanta reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray on a Venezuelan national detainee while housed in SDC in Lumpkin, Georgia. On April 24, 2024, the detainee refused to comply with SDC staff verbal commands, and in an aggressive manner, asserted his unwillingness when he told to remove a blanket that he was using to restrict the view into his housing unit. SDC staff administered one burst of OC spray, then administered another, followed by verbal com- mands to remove the blanket. SDC staff positioned the detainee on the ground and applied hand restraints. SDC staff escorted the detainee for decontamination and evaluation by medical staff. Detainee refused to enter decontamination shower. The medical unit did a visual assessment of the detainee as he was being uncooperative. Detainee was given verbal directions to decontaminate once placed in cell.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Chicago, Dodge County Detention Facility (DCDF)
narrative: On April 27, 2024, ERO Chicago reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray on a Syrian national detainee while housed at the DCDF in Juneau, Wisconsin. On April 26, 2024, the detainee refused orders to lock into his cell after taking a shower. DCDF reported that several DCDF staff attempted confrontational avoidance with the detainee, but the detainee would not comply with the orders. DCDF officers assembled a cell entry team for a calculated use of force. DCDF staff g utilized a pepper ball launcher one time into the day room but were unsuccessful in gaining compliance. The cell entry team entered the housing section and gained control of the detainee. The detainee received some minor scrapes on his arms and hip area. DCDF medical staff evaluated the detainee and placed him on  5-minute observation for his exposure to the OC. DCDF staff reported no injuries. ERO leadership and the Joint Intake Center were notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, Baker County Detention Center (BCDC)
narrative: On April 27, 2024, ERO Miami reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) on a Belizean national detainee housed at the BCDC in MacClenny, Florida. On April 26, 2024, BCDC staff advised the detainee that he would be receiving a disciplinary report for attempting to incite a disturbance. The detainee became upset and started denying attempts to incite a disturbance while agitated. BCDC staff attempted to de-escalate the situation, but the detainee remained agitated and refused verbal commands to submit to hand restraints. The detainee attempted to walk away, then reached over to the dorm door and snatched the privacy screen, while yelling and waving his hands trying to get the attention of the detainees inside the dorm. BCDC staff continued verbal commands and tried placing restraints on the detainee, he resisted by swinging his body to avoid getting hand cuffed and tried kicking his leg backwards at deputies. BCDC staff eventually placed restraints on the detainee and escorted | him to the BCDC Confinement Unit. Once in confinement, the detainee continued to resist BCDC staff when they tried to remove the hand restraints. BCDC staff gave the detainee several verbal commands which he refused. BCDC staff utilized a one second burst of OC spray to the detainee's facial area, and he immediately stopped resisting. BCDC staff escorted the detainee to the BCDC Medical Unit for decontamination and medical evaluation. No injuries were reported. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC), ICE Health
narrative: On April 27, 2024, ERO Miami reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray on a Jamaican national detainee while housed at the KSPC in Miami, Florida. On April 26, 2024, the detainee approached KSPC staff to make a complaint about another staff member. While providing the complaint, the detainee threatened the KSPC staff member in question, after which the supervisor notified the detainee that be would be taken to processing for threatening a KSPC staff member. The detainee would not comply with the KSPC staff member's verbal commands to cease his aggressive behavior. After several verbal commands, the detainee sat down and stated that he would not comply until he spoke to a higher-ranking supervisor or ERO Miami. A KSPC staff member then attempted custodial touch to stand up the detainee in order to submit to hand restraints, but the detainee became combative and while struggling, the detainee grabbed a KSPC staff member's hand restraint. KSPC staff deployed a single burst of OC spray to gain compliance and were able to apply hand restraints. KSPC staff members escorted the detainee to the shower area to decontaminate using copious amounts of water THSC medical staff assessed the detainee for post-use of force and was medically cleared. KSPC staff reported no injuries,

title: Use of Force

RCC medical staff decontaminated and completed medical assessments on the subject and reported no injuries to the subject or staff. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Atlanta, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Stewart Detention Center (SDC)

The detainee was placed in handcuffs and removed from the cell for decontamination but refused SDC staff orders to enter the shower area and refused to permit a medical evaluation or treatment by THSC staff. The detainee became combative and refused to comply with SDC staff orders to return to his cell, causing SDC staff to place the detainee in leg restraints for escort to his cell. The leg restraints and handcuffs were removed after the detainee was placed on his bed. No injuries were reported to the detainee or SDC staff, ERO Leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force

ERO leadership was notified. |

title: Use of Force

A Mexican national detainee, Ecuadorian national detainee, and a Guatemalan national detainee were transported to local hospitals for injuries sustained in the incident, and retumed to MVPC, and IHSC was notified of their return. title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Philadelphia, Moshannon Valley Processing Center (MVPC)

IHSC conducted a medical examination and ordered the detainee be transported to the FRH in Pearsall, Texas, for further medical examination. The detainee became aggressive and noncompliant upon arrival at the FRH. The detainee removed the hand restraint from his left hand, STIPC staff attempted to place the hand restraint back on and the detainee became more aggressive. STIPC staff took the detainee down and restrained the detainee due to continued refusal to comply with verbal commands. STIPC staff transported the detainee back to the STIPC and placed him in the Medical Housing Unit. At approximately 10:00 p.m. CST, the detainee broke the electrical outlet off the wall and tried to chew the electrical wires. STIPC staff moved the detainee to an isolation cell for suicide watch and STIPC staff ordered the detainee to place his hands through the tray door to remove the hands restraints. The detainee refused multiple commands to comply, STIPC staff deployed OC spray to gain compliance and a five-member officer team entered isolation and placed the detainee on the ground and in Jeg restraints. STIPC staff began the decontamination process and removed the leg and hand restraints from the detainee. THSC conducted a medical examination and reported the detainee did not sustain any injuries. participants: ERO Miami, Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC)

KSPC staff then gave verbal commands to the detainee to stop the aggression. KSPC staff then attempted to escort the detainee to the processing area to imitiate disciplinary proceedings. The detainee forcefully pulled away from the escorting staff and uttered verbal insults while actively resisting officers attempts to escort. Additional KSPC staff responded and utilized the required use of force to gain compliance. KSPC medical staff assessed the detainee and determined minor injuries were sustained. No injuries were reported from the staff. ERO leadership and the Joint Intake Center were notified

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO San Diego, Imperial Regional Detention (ICSO)
narrative: On February 29, 2024, ERO San Diego reported the use of force on a Canadian national housed in IRDF in Calexico, California. On February 28, 2024, the detainee was found scaling a perimeter fence to escape. ERO San Diego and IRDF staff gave the detainee verbal commands to get down onto the ground. The detainee failed to comply with verbal commands and turned to run. ERO San Diego and IRDF staff took the detainee down to the ground to apply hand and leg restraints. ERO San Diego applied the hand and leg restraints and transported the detainee back into the facility. IRDF staff escorted the detainee to medical for evaluation. No injuries were reported. The detainee will remain in the Medial Observation Housing Unit. ERO leadership and Joint Intake Center were notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC)
narrative: On March 1, 2024, ERO Miami reported the use of force on five detainees respectively from Dominica, Dominican Republic, Jamaica, and Nicaragua, during a brawl, while housed at the KSPC in Miami, Florida. A KSPC contract detention officer gave verbal commands to halt their combative behavior and attempted to physically separate the detainees, to no avail. The detainees created the 1-UOF when they remained noncompliant and continued their aggression. KSPC officers deployed their OC spray to neutralize the situation and gain compliance. Thereafter, KSPC officers were able to secure the detainees in hand restraints. Once restrained, all use of force ceased. KSPC detention officers then escorted the detainees to the KSPC processing shower area to effect decontamination utilizing copious amounts of water. IHSC medical staff assessed the detainees for post use of force clearance and medically cleared all detainees. KSPC officers reported secondary exposure _ to OC spray but no injuries. ERO leadership and the Joint Intake Center were notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Dallas, Prairieland Detention Center (PDC)
narrative: On March 2, 2024, ERO Dallas reported the use of force on a Nicaraguan national detainee while housed at the PDC in Alvarado, Texas. The detainee became physically aggressive during an escort to the medical unit for evaluation. PDC staff took the detainee to the ground to gain compliance. PDC staff referred the detainee for a mental health evaluation due to statements made during the incident. The detainee is pending medical evaluation. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO San Diego, Otay Mesa Detention Center (OMDC)
narrative: On Marcy 3, 2024, ERO San Diego reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray on a Panamanian national detainee while housed at the OMDC in San Diego, California. OMDC staff deployed a short burst of OC spray to the Panamanian national detainee to stop the altercation from continuing and separated both detainees. The other detainee was not exposed to OC. OMDC staff escorted the detainee to medical for evaluation and was cleared from the OC exposure, The detainee refused decontamination from OC and was given instructions on self-decontamination. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC)
narrative: On March 4, 2024, ERO Boston reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray on a Dominican national detainee while housed at the KSPC in Miami, Florida. On the same date, KSPC staff instructed the detainee to fix his uniform and comply with the detainee handbook regulations. KSPC staff gave additional verbal commands to the detainee to no avail. The detainee became physically aggressive towards KSPC staff and then KSPC staff deployed a burst of OC spray in order to gain compliance from the detainee. The detainee then lunged at the KSPC staff member with closed fists. A second burst of OC spray was deployed in order to gain control of the detainee. KSPC staff took the detainee to the ground, placed him in restraints, and gained compliance. KSPC staff escorted the detainee to the processing shower for decontamination. IHSC medical staff evaluated the detainee, noting no injuries. The KSPC staff member sustained no injuries. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Dallas, Prairieland Detention Center (PDC)
narrative: On March 5, 2024, ERO Dallas reported the use of force on a Georgian national detainee housed at the PDC in Alvarado, Texas. On March 4, 2024, the detainee, currently on suicide watch, cut himself on his upper left forearm with a piece of glass. PDC staff gave multiple verbal warnings and attempted to secure the glass from the detainee. The detainee became non- compliant, leading to the initiation of use of force protocols. PDC staff entered the detainee's cell to remove the piece of glass and took him to the ground. PDC staff successfully gained control and secured the detainee and placed him in restraints. PDC staff transferred the detainee to the Texas Health Huguley Hospital in Burleson, Texas, for a medical evaluation.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Dallas, Prairieland Detention Center (PDC)
narrative: On March 6, 2024, ERO Dallas reported the use of force on a Honduran national detainee housed at the PDC in Alvarado, Texas. On March 5, 2024, PDC staff gave multiple verbal warnings to the detainee after he attempted to interfere with PDC staff while they were dealing with another ICE detainee. PDC staff attempted to secure the detainee and he became non- compliant, leading to the initiation of use of force protocols. The detainee threw himself to the ground while being escorted to the segregation unit. PDC staff successfully gained control and secured the detainee with wrist restraints. PDC medical staff conducted an examination of the detainee and determined he did not sustain any injuries during the incident.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Denver, Denver Contract Detention Facility (DCDF), Aurora Police Department (APD), Lakewood Police Department (LPD)
narrative: On March 7, 2024, ERO Denver reported a use of force on a Mexican national detainee while house at DCDF in Aurora,Colorado. On March 6, 2024, the detainee refused to obey DCDF staff after he repeatedly banged on his door cell with hismattress and displayed aggressive behavior in his medical cell and covered the windows and camera of the cell. DCDF staffresponded and placed the detainee in a four-point restraint chair for his safety due to his verbal threats to hurt himself andothers. Once restrained, the detainee continued to be aggressive. DCDF staff verbally de-escalated the situation and releasedthe detainee from the restraint chair for transport to University of Colorado Hospital for further mental health treatment. EROLeadership, APD, LPD and the Joint Intake Center were notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO El Paso, Otero County Processing Center (OCPC)
narrative: On March 10, 2024, ERO El Paso reported the use of force on a Venezuelan national detainee while housed at the OCPC in Chaparral, New Mexico. On March 7, 2024, the detainee refused multiple OCPC staff orders to submit to hand restraints after becoming aggressive and combative. OCPC staff were able to deescalate and gain control of the situation. OCPC medical staff examined the detainee and reported no injuries. ERO El Paso and OCPC will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates, as necessary.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO San Antonio, South Texas ICE Processing Center (STIPC), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC)
narrative: On March 10, 2024, ERO San Antonio reported the use of force on a Kazakhstani national detainee while housed at STIPC in Pearsall, Texas. On March 9, 2024, the detainee was placed on suicide watch after threatening self-harm. STIPC staff ordered the detainee to change into a suicide gown and submit to hand restrains several times, but the detainee refused to comply with verbal commands. Five STIPC staff members entered the cell, placed the detainee on the ground, and applied hand restraints. STIPC staff escorted the detainee to the Special Management Unit and IHSC conducted a medical examination. No injuries to the detainee or STIPC staff members were reported. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC)
narrative: On March 11, 2024, ERO Miami reported the use of force on a Salvadoran national detainee while housed at the KSPC in Miami, Florida. On March 10, 2024, the detainee refused to follow multiple verbal commands given by IHSC medical staff to demonstrate the ingestion of daily medications, along with additional verbal commands to open his mouth to inspect. The detainee refused all attempts made by IHSC medical staff to comply. KSPC staff intervened to remove the detainee from the nursing station. The detainee physically resisted by kicking and shoving, with continued verbal threats. KSPC staff redirected the detainee onto the wall for hand restraint application, which he continued to resist. KSPC staff then redirected the detainee to the floor, applied restraints, and gained compliance. IHSC medical staff evaluated the detainee, noting no injuries. No injuries were reported to KSPC staff. KSPC staff will initiate disciplinary procedures.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO New Orleans, Central Louisiana ICE Correctional Center (CLIPC)
narrative: On March 13, 2024, ERO New Orleans reported the use of Oleoresin Capsicum (OC) on a Colombian national detainee while housed at CLIPC in Jena, Louisiana. On March 12, 2024, the detainee refused to remove paper coverings from his cell window and submit to restraints. CLIPC staff gave the detainee several verbal commands to remove to the coverings, but he refused to comply. CLIPC staff coordinated a calculated use of force, which consisted of deploying one two-second burst of OC spray into the detainee's cell though the cell door security hatch. CLIPC staff removed the detainee from his cell, initiated decontamination procedures, and referred him to medical staff for evaluation. The detainee refused medical assessment and CLIPC staff returned him to his cell after being decontaminated.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC)
narrative: On March 14, 2024, ERO Miami reported the use of force on a Dominican national detainee housed at the KSPC in Miami, Florida. KSPC staff issued verbal commands to halt their combative behavior and attempted to physically separate the detainees, which was ignored. KSPC staff separated the detainees, with the Dominican national detainee remaining noncompliant, resulting in KSPC staff placing the detainee on the ground and applying hand restraints. THSC assessed the detainee and recommended they be transported to a hospital due to possible head trauma from the incident. No injuries were reported from staff. ,

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Atlanta, Cobb County Adult Detention Center (CCADC), Stewart Detention Center (SDC)

On the same date, during transport of the detainee from the CCADC in Marietta, Geogia to the SDC; the detainee escaped from the transport vehicle. ERO Atlanta officers quickly apprehended the detainee. The detainee began to resist and was taken to the ground by ERO officers. The detainee reported he injured his knee after leaping from the moving vehicle. SDC medical staff evaluated the detainee who suffered abrasion injuries to his nght, upper arm. ERO Atlanta and Joint Intake Center were notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Dallas, Eden Detention Center (EDC)
narrative: On March 15, 2024, ERO Dallas reported the use of force on a Russian national detainee while housed at the EDC in Eden, Texas. On March 13, 2024, EDC staff observed the detainee engaging in self-harm while housed in restrictive housing EDC staff observed the detainee rapidly scraping the pointed end of a spork across his left forearm approximately midway up the inside of this forearm. The detainee failed to comply with multiple directives from security officers to cease engaging in self- harm. EDC Staff deployed inflammatory agents and the detainee ceased engaging in self-harm and became compliant. EDC staff removed the detainee from the cell and started the decontamination process. Medical staff evaluated the detainee and noted no injuries. Medical Staff placed the detainee on constant watch for suicide risk and self-harm ideation pending further investigation. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Harlingen, Webb County Detention (WCDC)
narrative: On March 15, 2024, ERO Harlingen reported the use of force, oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray, on five ICE detainees, one Ghatemala national, two Salvadoran nationals , one Mexico national, and one Venezuelan national, detainee housed at the WCDC in Laredo, Texas. On March 14, 2024, the detainees refused to return inside WCDC at the conclusion of recreation time, WCDC staff spoke with the detainees' multiple times over several hours, addressing their concerns while instructing them to return to their dormitory; however, the detainees refused to comply, WCDC deployed their Special Operations Response Team (SORT) to assist in returning the detainees back to their dormitory. As the SORT approached the detainees, they began to lock their arms together and shout. The SORT deployed OC spray on all five detainees and physically restrained them. WCDC escorted all detainees to the medical unit for decontamination and medical evaluation. WCDC medical personnel evaluated the five detainees and determined that they did not sustain any injuries. No injuries were reported by RGPC staff.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC)

The detainee actively resisted and became physically combative. KSPC staff took the detainee to the ground and deployed OC spray to gain compliance and stop the detainee from self-harm. KSPC staff placed the detainee against the wall to apply hand and leg restraints. Once restraints were placed, all use of force ceased. KSPC staff escorted the detainee to the processing shower for decontamination. TIHSC evaluated the detainee for injuries and recommended transportation to the hospital for a possible shoulder injury. KSPC staff were treated for secondary OC spray exposure, and one reported an elbow injury. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Washington, Immigration Centers of America (ICA)

title: Use of Force

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Harlingen, Rio Grande Processing Center (RGPC)

The detainee was decontaminated and escorted to the medical unit. The detainee was examined by RGPC medical staff and noted no injuries. No injuries were reported by RGPC staff.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC)

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC)
narrative: On January 26, 2024, ERO Miami reported the use of force on a Cuban national detainee housed at the KSPC in Miami, Florida. On January 25, 2024, KSPC staff were escorting the detainee to his housing unit when the detainee attempted to walk outside the designated escort path KSPC staff instructed the detainee numerous times to return to the designated escorting area, to which the detainee responded with profanity and racial slurs. The detainee returned to the escort area and KSPC staff applied hand restraints and escorted the detainee to processing for disciplinary proceedings. KSPC staff placed the detainee in a cell, and when one of the hand restraints were removed the detaince lunged as if to attempt to strike the KSPC staff. KSPC staff immediately applied the necessary force to redirect the detainee to the cell wall and reapplied the hand restraints while the . detainee continued to resist and attempt to kick the KSPC staff. The detainee ceased all aggression, and the restraints were removed. IHSC assessed the detainee and cleared him No injuries were reported from the staff. .

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO New Orleans, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Winn Correctional Center (WCC)
narrative: On January 27, 2024, ERO New Orleans reported the use of force and deployment of Oleoresin Capsicum (OC) spray on 126 detainees housed at the WCC in Winnfield, Louisiana. After the situation had been resolved WCC medical staff evaluated and completed medical assessments on all the detainees involved in this incident. WCC reported no * detainees were directly exposed to the OC spray. No medical treatment was provided, and all subjects were cleared of any issues. WCC staff notified ERO New Orleans of the use of force.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC)
narrative: On January 28, 2024, ERO Miami reported the use of force on a Mexican national detainee while housed at the KSPC in Miami, Florida, On January 27, 2024, KSPC staff observed the detainee at the KSPC cafeteria take an unauthorized amount of juice cartons. KSPC staff instructed the detainee to return the items. The detainee became verbally aggressive toward the KSPC staff. KSPC staff escort the detainee to the KSPC processing area to initiate disciplinary proceedings, while being escorted the detainee became angry and began to swing his arms and pull away. KSPC staff responded and utilized the required use of force to gain compliance and applied hand restraints. THSC assessed the detainee and medically cleared him. No injuries to KSPC staff were reported. ERO Leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO San Antonio, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), South Texas ICE Processing Center (STIPC)

STIPC staff took the detainee to the ground and applied hand and leg restraints to gain compliance. STIPC staff escorted the detainee to the medical unit for a medical evaluation and IHSC medical staff noted the detainee did not have any visual injuries, but will be places on suicide watch, due to threats of self-harm. title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Atlanta, Stewart Detention Center (SDC)
narrative: On January 29, 2024, ERO Atlanta reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray on a Honduran national detainee housed at the SDC in Lumpkin, Georgia. ERO Leadership was notified.

participants: ERO New Orleans, River Correctional Center (RCC)

RCC reported no detainees or staff were directly exposed to the OC deployment. No medical treatment was provided, and all detainees were cleared of any issues. Dorm security cameras recorded this spontaneous use of force, and the incident is currently under institutional review.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO San Diego, Imperial Regional Detention (ICSO)
narrative: On January 29, 2024, ERO San Diego reported the use of force on an Iraqi national detainee while housed at the IRDF in Calexico, California. On January 28, 2024, the IRDF officer posted in the segregated medical observation, activated a body alarm when the officer noticed the detainee had removed his clothing and was lying on the floor of the cell, unresponsive. When initial responders arrived, the cell door was opened to assess the detainee. The detainee quickly moved his nght hand and wrist between the cell door and door jamb preventing the cell door from being secured. IRDF officers obtained a plastic shield and utilized it to push the detainee back into the cell and placed him in restraints. IRDF medical staff conducted a brief assessment of the detainee and notated there were no signs of injury. IRDF responding officers reported no injuries. ERO leadership and the Joint Intake Center were notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO El Paso, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), El Paso Processing Center (EPC)
narrative: On January 30, 2024, ERO El Paso reported the use of force on a Venezuelan national detainee while housed at the EPPC in El Paso, Texas. On January 26, 2024, the detainee became combative toward a EPPC staff member when given verbal commands to keep moving as he walked to the mess hall. When EPPC staff asked the detainee for his identification, he stated that he did not have it in his possession, continued to argue with officers, and refused to proceed to the processing area to get a new identification card. An EPPC staff member proceeded to do a come along hold on the detainee and he became belligerent, pushed the EPPC staff member, and began to threaten him with bodily harm. EPPC staff successfully restrained the detainee, placed him in restraints and escorted him to processing. IHSC medical staff assessed the detainee for injuries and determined that he did not sustain any injuries. ERO El Paso and IHSC staff will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates, as necessary.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO El Paso, Cibola County Correctional Center (CCCC)
narrative: On February 1, 2024, ERO El Paso reported the use of force on three Venezuelan national detainees and one Colombian national detainee while housed at the CCCC in Milan, New Mexico. On January 31, 2024, 35 detainees refused to return to their housing unit at the conclusion of their recreation period on the recreation yard. The detainees stated they were dissatisfied with a national news report concerning immigration policy. ERO El Paso met with the group and convinced five detainees to return to their housing unit. CCCC staff executed an approved tactical operation and using minimum force to gain compliance of 26 detainees, CCCC Staff executed calculated use of force on the four remaining detainees, securing them in restraints, and escorting them to restrictive housing. CCCC medical staff evaluated and cleared the detainees.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO San Antonio, South Texas ICE Processing Center (STIPC), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC)
narrative: On February 2, 2024, ERO San Antonio reported the use of force on an Ecuadoran national detainee housed at the STIPC in Pearsall, Texas. On February 1, 2024, the detainee attempted to hit STIPC staff while being escorted through the hallway. STIPC staff immediately took the detainee down to the floor to apply leg restraints. STIPC staff placed the detainee on a gurney to escort to medical for evaluation. THSC medical staff evaluated the detainee and determined he sustained no injuries during the incident. The detainee will remain in medical isolation for observation. ERO Leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Dallas, Bluebonnet Detention Center (BBDC), Jones County Sheriff's Department (JCSD)
narrative: On February 3, 2024, ERO Dallas reported a use of force on a Colombian national detainee while housed at the BBDC in Anson, Texas, On February 2, 2024, BBDC staff referred the detainee to the medical department for a mental health evaluation. While in the mental health office, the detainee made threats to harm someone if he was not removed from the facility, BBDC security staff made verbal warnings to the detainee and attempted to place him in restraints when the detainee became physically aggressive. During the struggle, the detainee grabbed an electronic signature pen, stabbed a BBDC staff member under the chin and stabbed a second staff member near the cye, then attempting to bite them as well. BBDC staff successfully gained control of the detainee and placed him in restraints. Medical staff determined the detainee did not sustain any injuries. A police report was filed with the JCSO and ERO Leadership, and the Joint Intake Center were notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC)
narrative: On February 3, 2024, ERO Miami reported the use of force on a Haitian national detainee housed at the KSPC in Miami, Flor- ida. On February 2, 2024, the detainee approached and threatened to punch a KSPC staff member The KSPC staff attempted to question the detainee as to his erratic behavior, the detainee aggressively lunged at the KSPC staff member. To create distance, the KSPC staff member pushed him away, while a second KSPC staff member physically secured detainee and carried him outside the housing unit away from other detainees. The detainee continued uttering threats of inflicting bodily harm and remained noncompliant ignoring KSPC staff member's verbal commands to stop resisting and cease his aggressive behavior. Once outside the housing unit, additional KSPC staff arrived and assisted in redirecting the detainee to the wall and then ground to apply hand restraints and gain compliance. Once restrained, all use of force ceased. HSC medical staff assessed the detainee for post use of force clearance and recommended the detainee be transported to a local hospital in South Miami, Miami, FL, for further evaluation of elbow pain. KSPC staff involved in the use of force did not report any injuries. AGS management will initiate disciplinary procedures against the detainee. KSPC staff notified ERO Miami of the use of force. _

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC)

The detainee became irate and yelled profanities at the KSPC staff and then escalated the situation by aggressively lunging towards the KSPC staffs face with a closed fist. KSPC staff avoided the strike and redirected the detainee to the wall, causing him to then fall on the floor. Once on the floor, a second KSPC staff member applied hand and leg restraints to gain compliance. THSC assessed the detainee and cleared him. No injuries were reported from the staff. ERO leadership and the Joint Intake Center were notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO New Orleans, Central Louisiana ICE Correctional Center (CLIPC)
narrative: On February 6, 2024, ERO New Orleans reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray on two Venezuelan national detainees housed in CLIPC Jena, Louisiana. The second detainee joined in kicking the fence and CLIPC staff deployed a single burst of oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray on the two detainees to regain compliance. CLIPC staff secured all detainees in hand restraints and escorted them to medical for decontamination and assessment after the exposure. ERO leadership and the Joint Intake Center have been notified.

title: Use of Force

narrative: On March 27, 2024, ERO Miami reported the use of force on a Honduran national detainee housed in KSPC in Miami, Florida. On March 26, 2024, the detainee refused to cease his disruptive behavior while actively involved in a physical confrontation with another detainee, within the confines of the KSPC cafeteria. Once restraints were placed, all use of force ceased. KSPC staff escorted the detainee for medical evaluation. IHSC evaluated the detainee for injuries and medically cleared him. KSPC staff did not report any injuries. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force

The detainee sustained no injuries during the use of force. A few MVPC staff members sustained minor injuries. ERO leadership and Joint Intake Center were notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC)
narrative: On August 10, 2024, ERO Miami reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray on two Dominican national detainees and one Haitian national while housed at the KSPC in Miami, Florida, On August 8, 2024, the detainees were involved in a physical altercation and after several verbal orders to stop and attempts to separate the detainees failed, two KSPC detention officers (DOs) deployed two separate wide burst of OC spray into the nexus area of the fighting. Post-OC deployment, all detainees ceased fighting, disengaged, and were placed in restraints. KSPC DOs escorted the detainees to the KSPC processing shower area for decontamination, and an evaluation by IHSC medically cleared two of the detainees. The third detainee was transported to a local hospital for injuries to his lips and foot. No KSPC DOs were injured during the incident. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO El Paso, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), El Paso Processing Center (EPC)
narrative: On August 11, 2024, ERO El Paso reported the use of force on a Cuban national detainee housed at the EPPC in El Paso, Texas. EPPC staff placed the detainee in a single cell. The detainee was examined by IHSC and medically cleared with no injuries reported. ERO El Paso and IHSC staff will continue to monitor the detainee and will provide updates, as necessary. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Harlingen, Valley Baptist Medical Center (VBMC)

No injuries were reported to the detainee or VBMC staff. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC)

The detainee began striking his head against a bulletin board, causing KSPC staff to take the detainee to the floor and apply hand restraints to gain compliance. IHSC staff examined the detainee and reported no injuries, and no injuries were reported by KSPC staff. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Miami, Krome Service Processing Center (KSPC), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC)

The detainees were examined by IHSC staff and noted no injuries. KSPC staff did not report any injuries. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO El Paso, ICE Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), El Paso Processing Center (EPC)
narrative: On August 13, 2024, ERO El Paso reported the use of force on a Venezuelan national detainee housed at the EPC in El Paso, Texas. On August 11, 2024, the detainee was involved in an altercation with other detainees. An EPC officer approached the detainee and requested his identification, to which he refused. The detainee failed to comply after multiple attempts and made verbal threats. EPC officers placed an escort hold to remove the detainee from the unit due to his participation, but the detaince actively resisted. EPC officers secured the detainee's arms and placed him to the floor to be restrained, but the detainee continued to be combative and kicked an EPC officer in the face/nose area. EPC officers were able to secure the detainee's legs until additional officers arrived and successfully applied hand restraints. Once restrained, the detainee was assisted to his feet and escorted to processing. EPC officers placed the detainee in a single cell and IHSC cleared him of any injuries. EPC officers reported no significant injuries. ERO El Paso referred the incident to OPR, and the case is currently under review, pending criminal prosecution for assault on an officer. ERO El Paso and IHSC staff will continue to monitor the detainee and provide updates, as necessary. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO El Paso, ICE Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR), ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), El Paso Processing Center (EPC)
narrative: On August 13, 2024, ERO El Paso reported the use of force on a Salvadoran national detainee while housed at the EPC in El Paso, Texas. EPC officers attempted to restrain the detainee, but they broke away and struck an officer with a closed fist on the left side of the face and scratched another officer on the left side of his face. EPC officers secured the detainee's arms and took him down to the floor to regain control. Hand restraints were applied, and the detainee was escorted to processing. The detainee actively resisted escorting and EPC staff officers applied a wrist lock on both wrists and continued to escort him to processing. The detainee was placed in a single cell and IHSC cleared him of injuries. EPC officers reported no significant injuries. ERO El Paso referred the incident to OPR, and the case is currently under review, pending criminal prosecution for assault on an officer. ERO El Paso and IHSC staff will continue to monitor the detainee and provide updates, as necessary. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force

title: Use of Force

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO San Antonio, ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), South Texas ICE Processing Center (STIPC)
narrative: On August 14, 2024, ERO San Antonio reported the use of force on a Cuban national detainee while housed at the STIPC in Pearsall, Texas. STIPC immediately grabbed the detainee and took him down to the floor and gained compliance. IHSC conducted a medical examination and noted no injuries. Staff members removed the hand restraints and placed the detainee back in his cell without further incident. There were no injuries reported by STIPC staff. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Atlanta, Stewart Detention Center (SDC)
narrative: On August 15, 2024, ERO Atlanta reported the use of oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray on a Venezuelan national while boused at the SDC in Lumpkin, Georgia. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force

title: Use of Force

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Philadelphia, Moshannon Valley Processing Center (MVPC)

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Philadelphia, Moshannon Valley Processing Center (MVPC), ICE Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR)
narrative: On August 20, 2024, ERO Philadelphia reported the use of force and deployment on an Egyptian national detainee, a Gambian national detainee, a Dominican national detainee, and a Jamaican national detainee while housed at MVPC in Philipsburg, Pennsylvania. The Egyptian detainee has multiple contusions to the head and torso, and possible laceration to the shoulder. The Gambian detainee has a stab wound to the abdomen. The Jamaican detainee has head trauma, a large contusion on his face, and a stab wound beside his nose. The Dominican detainee has a suspected dislocation of the shoulder. Three of the detainees were transported to Penn Highlands Hospital Dubois, m Dubois, Pennsylvania, and returned to MVPC. The fourth detainee was transported to Penn Highlands Hospital Clearfield, in Clearfield, Pennsylvania, and is pending a surgical consult. ERO leadership and the OPR Intake Center were notified.

title: Use of Force

title: Use of Force

KSPC staff pinned the detainee to the wall, but the detainee continued to kick and strike the KSPC staff with a closed fist. title: Use of Force

title: Use of Force

The detainee was ordered to submit to hand restraints and initially began to comply. The detainee's cell mate told him not to comply and he stopped complying with TDHDC officers. TDHDC officers used the minimal amount of force necessary to take the detainee to the ground and placed him in hand restraints. The detainee was escorted to the Restricted Housing Unit (RHU) and placed him in cell RHU 105. The detainee's cell mate became verbally aggressive and refused TDHDC officers orders to submit to hand restraints. TDHDC officers used the minimal! amount of force to take the detainee to the ground and placed him in hand restraints. TDHDC officers escorted him to cell RHU 106. IHSC attempted to conduct a medical evaluation for both detainees, but they both refused treatment and claimed no injuries. IHSC evaluated the other detainees involved in the altercation and no injuries were found. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force

EVDF medical staff evaluated the detainee and reported no injuries. ERO leadership was notified.

title: Use of Force

title: Use of Force

As CLIPC staff attempted to enter the cell, the detainee swung the sock containing the hard object, which struck a CLIPC staff member in the arm and caused some bruising. CLIPC staff subsequently enter the cell, secured, and removed the detainee from his cell. The detainee was decontaminated and referred to medical and mental bealth staff for evaluation. title: Use of Force

title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Phoenix, Central Arizona Florence Correctional Complex (CAFCC)
narrative: On October 5, 2024, ERO Phoenix reported the deployment of Oleoresin Capsicum (OC) spray on a Honduran national detainee while housed at the CAFCC in Florence, Arizona. title: Use of Force
participants: ERO Philadelphia, Clinton County Correctional Facility (CCCF), University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC)
narrative: On November 2, 2024, ERO Philadelphia reported the use of force, oleoresin capsicum (OC) spray and an electro muscular psa device (TASER) on a Dominican national detainee while housed at the CCDF in McElhattan, Pennsylvania. On the same date, the detainee tied a sheet to the top portion of his bed in his cell, climbed on top of the bed, and attempted to place the sheet around his neck. The detainee failed to comply with CCCF orders to drop the sheet and get off the bed and stated he intended to kill himself, causing CCCF staff to enter the cell and attempt to cut the sheet away from the bed and physically restrain the detainee. The detainee physically resisted CCCF staff, causing CCCF staff to deploy OC spray to gain compliance. The detainee began displaying symptoms of a seizure and was transported to medical for evaluation. The detainee was subsequently transported by emergency medical services to UPMC in Jersey Shore, Pennsylvania for evaluation. UPMC medically cleared the detainee, and CCCF staff transported the detainee to CCCF. The detainee physically resisted CCCF staff when being placed in a padded cell for suicide watch, causing CCCF staff to use a TASER on the detainee to gain compliance. CCCF staff placed the detainee on the floor, changed the detainee into a suicide smock and placed the detainee into a padded cell for suicide watch. ERO leadership and the ICE OPR Joint Intake Center were notified.

title: Use of Force

Once restrained, all use of force was ceased. KSPC staff escorted the detainees to the showers to decontaminate. IHSC staff assessed the detainee and medically cleared him.
